about: The per-peak state the user edits and the views read: dragged label positions, selection, which peaks are annotated, mode labels (the user's own and the auto-detected), the one definitive Air/Top/Back and the tap-tone ratio, and what clears it all. Each case starts a fresh analyzer, sets its 'type' (a guitar type, by saved name) as Settings does, and loads its 'files.measurement' as the app loads a file — the peaks (classified by the analyzer under that type), their selection, Show Unknown Modes — then runs its 'steps'. 'peakIds' gives each case-local peak name its id (a name not in the file is a peak the analyzer does not know). Steps: the shared steps of tooling/analyzer-steps (settings, newTap), and {"load": file}; {"toggle": name} (a click on a peak); {"selectNone": true}; {"resetToAuto": true} (the wand); {"override": [name, label]} (a label of the user's); {"resetOverride": name} (Reset to Auto); {"offset": [name, Hz, dB]} (a dragged label); {"resetOffset": name}; {"resetAllOffsets": true} (Reset Labels); {"visibility": all | selected | none}; {"cycleVisibility": true} (the annotations button); {"guitarTypeChange": type} (Settings changes the guitar type and applies it); {"check": {...}} asserts those fields at that point. Fields: 'selected' (names, any order), 'userModified', 'visible' (the annotated peaks' Hz, ascending), 'visibility', 'savedVisibility' (the visibility the settings hold — what the next launch uses), 'label' / 'mode' / 'autoMode' / 'manualOverride' (per name; mode is override-aware, autoMode is not; modes by Swift's case name: air, top, back, dipole, ringMode, upperModes, unknown), 'overrides' (the whole map, name → label), 'offsets' (the whole map, name → [Hz, dB]), 'offsetCount', 'getPeak' (mode → name or null), 'hasRatio', 'definitive' (air/top/back → {hz, isOverride} or null), 'selectedIsAuto' (the selection is the automatic one), 'materialPeakMode' (the mode of a plate/brace capture's fL peak). AS41 starts from no file: a brace capture, through the shared steps. Expected values are Swift's.
